steps.message:
Item 051 on the Package A verification register is assigned to me and falls due on 07/20/2026, two days before the Level-3 placement. It covers the Block C spread footings and the long-term settlement of the clay beneath them.

Work through Item 051 against the project record and issue the verification memo. Set out what you reviewed, the basis you applied, your findings with the working behind them, and the disposition. Where something has to be produced before the item can be closed, say what it is and who is required to produce it.

Use the attached memorandum form and keep its sections. Write it from Rahul Nimkar, Geotechnical Reviewer, to Adrian Vance, Project Engineer, copied to Rachel Marlbeck. Save it as Thelbridge_Verification_Memo_Item051_BlockC.docx.

1.  EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Kelbrook Geotechnical, Inc. has completed a subsurface investigation and geotechnical engineering analysis for
Package A of the Birchwood Village Expansion Program at 1802 Larchwood Avenue, Columbus, Ohio.
Package A comprises three student-housing blocks (Blocks A, B and C) constructed over a shared podium, with
a single basement level beneath Blocks A and B, and a separate deep plant-room excavation planned beneath
Block B.
The finished design grade across Package A is established at El. 750.0 ft. Existing ground surface stands at
approximately El. 750.0 across the footprints of Blocks A and C but falls to about El. 738.0 across the Block B
footprint (a former surface drainage swale). Placement of engineered fill of variable thickness — up to
approximately 12 ft beneath Block B — will therefore be required to bring the site to design grade.
The subsurface profile consists of three principal strata:
•  Stratum 1 — Upper sand, classified SP-SM (poorly-graded sand with silt), medium-dense, from
existing grade down to El. 738.0, total unit weight 118 pcf.
•  Stratum 2 — Compressible clay aquitard, classified CL (lean clay of medium plasticity),
normally-consolidated, from El. 738.0 down to El. 720.0 (18 ft thick), total unit weight 120 pcf, low
permeability. This is the strata governing settlement of shallow foundations and provides the aquitard
between the shallow and deep groundwater regimes.
•  Stratum 3 — Dense sand and gravel aquifer, classified SW-GW, below El. 720.0, total unit weight 130
pcf, confined by the overlying clay.
Groundwater is present as two distinct regimes:
•  The design water table in the upper sand is set at El. 742.0 ft. Piezometer readings taken from three
shallow standpipes over the 11/2024–02/2025 monitoring period range from El. 741.6 to El. 742.4;
groundwater seepage was observed at El. 741.8 to El. 742.2 in the Block A test-pit excavation.
•  A confined piezometric head of El. 738.0 ft has been measured in the deep sand-and-gravel aquifer
through two deep piezometers screened below El. 720.0, with readings ranging El. 737.7 to El. 738.3. The
confined head is at essentially the same elevation as the top of the clay aquitard.
Consolidation testing on two undisturbed Shelby-tube samples of the compressible clay (samples B-06 U3 and
B-08 U2, tested per ASTM D2435) yielded a compression index Cc = 0.28, a recompression index Cr = 0.045,
an initial void ratio e0 = 0.92, an in-situ vertical effective stress σ'0 = 1,850 psf, and a preconsolidation pressure
σ'p = 1,900 psf. The margin (σ'p − σ'0 ≈ 50 psf) confirms the clay is essentially normally-consolidated: any net
stress increase applied at the top of the clay will produce virgin (Cc) compression rather than recompression
(Cr) compression.
Principal geotechnical recommendations are as follows:
1.  Block C — Spread footings may be founded within the upper sand. Consolidation of the underlying
compressible clay under column-load stress increases at mid-depth of the clay must be explicitly computed
by the Structural Engineer of Record, using the parameters provided herein, and reconciled against the
settlement tolerances specified in the project structural criteria.
2.  Blocks A and B basement mat — A conventional reinforced-concrete mat foundation may be founded
within the upper sand at the design underside elevation. Hydrostatic uplift from the El. 742.0 water table
must be resolved by mat self-weight, superimposed permanent loads and, where necessary, tension
elements. The waterproofing system for the below-grade envelope must be selected for the applicable

3.2  Regional and Local Geology
Columbus, Ohio lies within the Till Plains section of the Central Lowland physiographic province. Regional
surficial geology is dominated by Wisconsinan-age glacial deposits — chiefly clay-rich till, glaciolacustrine silt
and clay, and outwash sand and gravel — overlying Devonian-age carbonate and shale bedrock. Local
hydrogeology is characterized by a shallow phreatic surface within the outwash and reworked outwash sands, a
laterally continuous fine-grained aquitard, and a lower confined aquifer within basal outwash sand and gravel
above bedrock.
The subsurface conditions encountered in the Package A borings are consistent with this regional framework: a
medium-dense reworked outwash sand at the surface, a low-permeability clay of glaciolacustrine origin at
intermediate depth, and a dense outwash sand and gravel aquifer at depth. Bedrock was not encountered within
the maximum boring depth of 90 ft (approximately El. 660.0). Blow counts in the SW-GW below El. 720.0
were consistently in the range N ≥ 50 blows per 6 inches, indicating a very dense sand-and-gravel deposit
suitable as a pile-bearing stratum.

and later editions), and Thornbury State University campus master planning archives — indicates that the

The Block B footprint is raised approximately 12 ft above its natural surface by engineered fill placed

Deep foundations driven from the raised working grade pass through that consolidating layer. Where the
surrounding soil settles more than the pile, the relative movement at the pile-soil interface reverses:

Over the depth in which that condition applies the interface shear acts downward on the pile. It is an
additional axial load carried by the pile, not a component of its resistance, and it is superimposed on
the structural load for as long as consolidation continues.
The magnitude depends on the thickness of the still-consolidating layer, the interface shear available
within it and the depth of the neutral plane. Requirements for its treatment in design are set out in

Strength design (LRFD) load combinations for gravity, wind, and seismic follow ASCE 7-16 §2.3.1. Allowable

P6: 'Field Memorandum — Level-2 Concrete Strength Non-Conformance (Set 3, Mix 03-CD-A)'
P7: ''
P8: ''
P9: '1. Purpose'
P10: "On review of the 07/06/2026 laboratory reports for the Level-2 slab, mix 03-CD-A specified at 5,000 psi, Set 3 (cast 05/26/2026) returned a 28-day average of 4,620 psi and a 7-day break of 3,150 psi. Both results fall below the specified f'c of 5,000 psi. Cylinder 4,180 psi is a failing individual test. In accordance with ACI 318-19 §26.12.3.1, we are treating Set 3 as a non-conforming placement and recommend rejection pending core testing."
P11: '2. Placement and Sample Reference'
P12: ''
P13: '3. Result Summary'
P14: ''
P15: "Specified strength: 5,000 psi. All three broken cylinders returned strengths below f'c. The 4,180 psi 28-day cylinder is a failing individual test. The 3,150 psi break at 7 days confirms early-age deficiency in the same placement. The 4,620 psi 28-day average is 380 psi below the 5,000 psi specified strength."
P16: '4. Basis for Non-Conformance'
P17: 'Set 3 of mix 03-CD-A is non-conforming to Specification 03 30 00 Article 3.7 and to ACI 318-19 §26.12.3.1. The 28-day average of 4,620 psi does not meet the 5,000 psi requirement, and the 4,180 psi individual break is a further failing result. Set 3 is accordingly flagged as a non-conforming placement.'
P18: '5. Recommended Disposition'
P19: 'Reject Set 3 as placed pending confirmation by in-place core testing. We propose to core the placement per ACI 318-19 §26.12.3.4 after Thelbridge concurrence. Coring locations will be coordinated with Vantree Materials Testing and with Karen Tarbray so that neither the Level-2 slab surface finishes nor the Level-3 shoring layout is disturbed ahead of the 07/22/2026 Level-3 placement hold-point.'
P20: '6. Schedule Impact'
P21: 'The Level-3 concrete placement is scheduled for 07/22/2026 (contractual hold-point). Coring, cure, and break time for three cores is on the order of 5–7 working days from the day cores are drilled. If coring authorization is issued this week, results can be in the record before the 07/22/2026 pour. Any slip in Thelbridge concurrence pushes the Level-3 hold-point at risk.'
P22: 'Please advise on Owner and Thelbridge concurrence at the earliest.'

steps.message:
I have completed the geotechnical verification review of **Item 051** on the Package A Verification Register and issued the verification memorandum using the attached Thelbridge memorandum template.

### Deliverable Produced
- **File Path**: `/filesystem/Thelbridge_Verification_Memo_Item051_BlockC.docx`
- **Format & Header**: Preserves all five template sections (`1. PURPOSE`, `2. DOCUMENTS REVIEWED`, `3. BASIS OF REVIEW`, `4. FINDINGS`, `5. CONCLUSION AND RECOMMENDATION`) and signature block, addressed from **Rahul Nimkar, Geotechnical Reviewer** (`Thelbridge Project Management Services`) to **Adrian Vance, Project Engineer** (`Thelbridge Project Management Services`), copied to **Rachel Marlbeck, University Program Director** (`Thornbury State University`), dated **07/20/2026**.

---

### Summary of Review and Key Results

1. **Documents Reviewed & Governing Basis**:
   - Reviewed `KGI-2024-0417 Rev. 2` (*Geotechnical Investigation Report*, 02/14/2025) and Appendix A (*Boring Logs and Groundwater Monitoring Record B-01 through B-09*, issued 06/30/2026), `VMT-2025-0109-CON` (*ASTM D2435 1D Consolidation Test Data*, 01/09/2025), `VMT-2024-0917-PkgA-INDEX` (*Geotechnical Index Test Data*, 01/09/2025), `CB-GEO-007 Rev. 0` (*Block C Spread Footing Settlement*, 09/30/2025), `CB-DBM-001 Rev. 2` (*Design Basis Memorandum*, 11/14/2025), Structural Drawings `S-101 Rev. 4` and `S-201 Rev. 4` (05/29/2026), `Specification Section 31 20 00 Rev. 3` (*Earth Moving*, 03/06/2026), `SM-BLKC-2026-Rev14.xlsx` (*Settlement Monitoring Records — Block C*, Rounds 1–15 from 12/12/2025 through 06/26/2026), `Thelbridge_Verification_Register_PkgA.xlsx` (anchor date 07/15/2026, Items 041 and 051), and supporting program minutes/correspondence (`07/06/2026` Owner Verification Directive, `07/09/2026` Progress Meeting Minutes No. 26, `07/14/2026` Level-3 Pour Readiness email).
   - Applied the governing tolerances of `Specification Section 31 20 00` Article 3.6.A (**$1.0\text{ in}$ maximum total settlement**; **$0.5\text{ in}$ maximum differential settlement over $30\text{ ft}$**), `CB-DBM-001 Rev. 2` Section 7.3, and `CB-GEO-007` Sheet 1 (**$1/500$ maximum angular distortion** between adjacent columns), together with the mandatory requirement of `KGI-2024-0417 Rev. 2` Sections 1, 8.1, and 9.1 that one-dimensional primary consolidation of the 18-ft-thick Stratum 2 (CL) clay aquitard (El. 738.0 to El. 720.0 ft; $H = 18.0\text{ ft} = 216.0\text{ in}$, double-drained $H_{dr} = 9.0\text{ ft}$, $C_c = 0.28$, $C_r = 0.045$, $e_0 = 0.92$, $\sigma'_0 = 1,850\text{ psf}$, $\sigma'_p = 1,900\text{ psf}$, $\text{OCR} = 1.03$, $c_v = 4.4 \times 10^{-4}\text{ cm}^2/\text{s} \approx 0.041\text{--}0.042\text{ ft}^2/\text{day}$) be explicitly computed under $\Delta\sigma = 900\text{ psf}$ at mid-depth of the clay (El. 729.0 ft).

2. **Findings and Supporting Working**:
   - **Finding 1 — Omission of Primary Consolidation in `CB-GEO-007`**: Although the EOR transcribed all Stratum 2 clay consolidation parameters onto `CB-GEO-007` Sheet 2 (`INPUT`) and Sheet 5 (`Inputs`), **Sheet 4 (`Consolidation`) was left completely blank (`"—"`)** with the note *"Not computed. Serviceability taken from the immediate settlement result on Sheet 3."* Sheet 3 (`Schmertmann`) evaluated only short-term elastic/undrained settlement ($S_i = 0.70\text{ to }0.90\text{ in}$, $\Delta S_i = 0.20\text{ in}$).
   - **Finding 2 — Primary Consolidation ($S_c$) and Total Settlement ($S_{\text{total}}$) Exceed the 1.0-in Tolerance by 5.1× to 6.3×**:
     With $\frac{C_c H}{1 + e_0} = \frac{0.28 \times 216\text{ in}}{1.92} = 31.500\text{ in}$ ($2.625\text{ ft}$) and $\frac{C_r H}{1 + e_0} = \frac{0.045 \times 216\text{ in}}{1.92} = 5.0625\text{ in}$:
     - *Method A (GIR §8.1 normally-consolidated formula from $\sigma'_0 = 1,850\text{ psf}$ to $\sigma'_f = 2,750\text{ psf}$)*:
       $$S_c = 31.500\text{ in} \times \log_{10}\left(\frac{1,850 + 900}{1,850}\right) = 31.500 \times 0.172161 = \mathbf{5.42\text{ in}}\ (0.452\text{ ft})$$
     - *Method B (Two-branch bi-linear recompression from $1,850 \rightarrow 1,900\text{ psf}$ + virgin compression from $1,900 \rightarrow 2,750\text{ psf}$)*:
       $$S_c = 5.0625\log_{10}\left(\frac{1,900}{1,850}\right) + 31.500\log_{10}\left(\frac{2,750}{1,900}\right) = 0.059 + 5.058 = \mathbf{5.12\text{ in}}\ (0.426\text{ ft})$$
     - *Method C (Single-branch virgin compression referenced to $\sigma'_p = 1,900\text{ psf}$, $\sigma'_f = 2,800\text{ psf}$)*:
       $$S_c = 31.500\text{ in} \times \log_{10}\left(\frac{1,900 + 900}{1,900}\right) = 31.500 \times 0.168404 = \mathbf{5.30\text{ in}}\ (0.442\text{ ft})$$
     - Combined with the EOR's immediate settlement $S_i = 0.90\text{ in}$ at governing interior footing F-C6 ($0.82\text{ in}$ at F-C7), total long-term settlement reaches **$S_{\text{total}} = S_i + S_c = 6.02\text{ to }6.32\text{ in}$** at F-C6 (**$5.94\text{ to }6.24\text{ in}$** at F-C7), exceeding the **$1.0\text{ in}$** maximum total settlement limit by more than sixfold.
   - **Finding 3 — Long-Term Differential Settlement and Angular Distortion Exceed Tolerances ($0.5\text{ in}$ and $1/500$)**:
     - Between governing interior footing F-C6 ($\Delta\sigma = 900\text{ psf}$, $S_c = 5.42\text{ in}$ [NC] / $5.12\text{ in}$ [bi-linear], $S_i = 0.90\text{ in}$, $S_{\text{total}} = 6.32 / 6.02\text{ in}$) and corner footing F-C12 ($\Delta\sigma_{2:1} = 628.6\text{ psf}$, $S_c = 4.00 / 3.70\text{ in}$, $S_i = 0.70\text{ in}$, $S_{\text{total}} = 4.70 / 4.40\text{ in}$), differential consolidation settlement is **$\Delta S_c = 1.42\text{ in}$** ($1.17\text{--}1.21\text{ in}$ single-footing 2:1) and combined differential settlement is **$\Delta S_{\text{total}} = 1.37\text{ to }1.62\text{ in}$** (**$2.7\times\text{ to }3.2\times$** the $0.5\text{ in}$ limit).
     - Between orthogonally adjacent columns spaced at $L = 24.0\text{ ft} = 288\text{ in}$ ($< 30\text{ ft}$ reference span), $\Delta S_{\text{total}}$ reaches **$1.00\text{ to }1.45\text{ in}$** for F-C7 vs. F-C11 (angular distortion **$\beta = 1/288\text{ to }1/199 > 1/500$**), **$0.93\text{ in}$** for F-C8 vs. F-C12 ($\beta = 1/310 > 1/500$), and **$0.79\text{ in}$** for F-C6 vs. F-C2 ($\beta = 1/365 > 1/500$). Under the empirical spatial distribution ratio already observed in the field ($S_{\text{MP-12}} / S_{\text{MP-7}} = 50.8\%$), long-term differential settlement will reach **$2.27\text{ to }3.11\text{ in}$**.
   - **Finding 4 — Correlation with 06/26/2026 Field Monitoring Reading ($-0.61\text{ in}$) and Terzaghi Time-Rate**:
     - At Round 15 (`06/26/2026`, $t = 196\text{ days}$ after the `12/12/2025` post-footing baseline), cumulative settlement reached **$-0.61\text{ in}$ at MP-7** ($-0.58\text{ in}$ at MP-6; $-0.31\text{ in}$ at MP-12). Measured differential settlement is already **$0.30\text{ in}$** diagonally (MP-7 vs. MP-12) and **$0.23\text{ in}$** orthogonally over $24.0\text{ ft}$ (MP-7 vs. MP-3; MP-8 vs. MP-12)—already exceeding the EOR's $0.20\text{ in}$ total differential prediction and reaching $60\%$ of the $0.5\text{ in}$ tolerance.
     - The 14-day settlement increment at MP-7 has accelerated continuously from **$-0.03\text{ in / 14 days}$** (Rounds 2–4) to **$-0.07\text{ in / 14 days}$** ($-0.0050\text{ in/day} \approx -1.83\text{ in/yr}$) in Round 15.
     - With double drainage ($H_{dr} = 9.0\text{ ft}$) and $c_v = 0.042\text{ ft}^2/\text{day}$ ($4.5 \times 10^{-4}\text{ cm}^2/\text{s}$), primary consolidation requires **$t_{50} = 380\text{ days}$ ($1.04\text{ yr}$, $T_v = 0.197$)** for $50\%$ consolidation and **$t_{90} = 1,635\text{ days}$ ($4.48\text{ yr}$, $T_v = 0.848$)** for $90\%$ consolidation ($t_{95} = 5.96\text{ yr}$). Under progressive ramp loading over 196 days ($t_{\text{eff}} \approx 98\text{ days}$, $T_{v,\text{eff}} = 0.0508$, $U_{\text{eff}} = 25.4\%$) at partial dead load (~35%–45% of full service $D+L$), the observed $-0.61\text{ in}$ represents only **~10%–12% of the ultimate settlement**, with **~88%–90% ($\sim 5.4\text{--}5.7\text{ in}$)** still to occur. At the current velocity, the $1.0\text{ in}$ total limit will be breached in **$78\text{ days}$ (~09/12/2026)** and the $0.5\text{ in}$ differential limit in **$93\text{ days}$ (~09/27/2026)**.
   - **Finding 5 — Unreconciled Geometry & Sublayer Discrepancies**: `CB-GEO-007` Sheet 2 models footing underside at **El. 740.5 ft** ($8.5'\times 8.5'$ to $10.5'\times 10.5'$, matching `Settlement_Monitoring_BlockC.xlsx` Sheet 2), whereas Drawing `S-201 Rev. 4` Detail 3/S-201 shows underside at **El. 746.0 ft** ($7'-6"\times 7'-6"\times 2'-0"$); additionally, `CB-GEO-007` Sheet 3 models $5.25\text{ ft}$ of Stratum 1 sand below El. 740.5 ft despite Stratum 2 clay starting at El. 738.0 ft ($2.50\text{ ft}$ below El. 740.5 ft).

3. **Disposition and Required Deliverables Before Item 051 Can Be Closed**:
   - **Disposition**: **`NOT VERIFIED`** (Register status remains **`Open`**).
   - **Deliverables Required Prior to Closure and Responsible Parties**:
     1. **Formal Written Notification to EOR & Written Load-Application Hold Notice on Block C** — Required from **Adrian Vance, Project Engineer, Thelbridge Project Management Services** (copied to **Rachel Marlbeck, Thornbury State University**) per `Spec 31 20 00` Art. 3.6.B and the `07/06/2026` Owner Verification Directive, notifying the EOR of the settlement exceedance and directing the Contractor that no additional load (including any Level-3 placement loading tributary to Block C) may be applied until a written disposition and remedial design are verified.
     2. **Revised, Signed, and Sealed Calculation `CB-GEO-007` (`Rev. 1`) & Reconciled Drawings (`S-101` / `S-201 Rev. 5`)** — Required from **Gregory Nash, PE (Engineer of Record) and M. Halbrook, PE (Checker), Calloway Braddock Structural Engineers, LLC**, completing Sheet 4 (`Consolidation`), combining $S_i + S_c$, correcting Sheet 3 sublayer geometry, and reconciling the footing elevation/dimension discrepancy.
     3. **Written Engineering Disposition, Existing-Frame Distortion Assessment, and Sealed Remedial Foundation Design Package** — Required from **Gregory Nash, PE, Calloway Braddock Structural Engineers, LLC** (in coordination with **Alden Roscombe, PE, Kelbrook Geotechnical, Inc.**) per `Spec 31 20 00` Art. 3.6.B and `KGI-2024-0417 Rev. 2` §9.1, providing a sealed remedial foundation design (e.g., micropile/jacked-pile underpinning to Stratum 3 SW-GW below El. 720.0 ft or mat/grade-beam conversion) that arrests primary consolidation and maintains post-remediation total/differential settlements within $1.0\text{ in}$ / $0.5\text{ in}$ / $1/500$, plus a structural distortion check of existing Block C framing, podium interface, and CMU partitions for the $0.61\text{ in}$ total / $0.30\text{ in}$ differential movement incurred to date.
     4. **Signed and Sealed Geotechnical Concurrence Memorandum on Remedial Foundation Design** — Required from **Alden Roscombe, PE, Kelbrook Geotechnical, Inc.**, verifying Stratum 3 bearing/bond parameters, Stratum 2 negative skin friction/downdrag allowances, and confined-aquifer piezometric head (El. 738.0 ft) aquitard sealing procedures per `KGI-2024-0417 Rev. 2` §§9.1 and 9.6.
     5. **Written Load-Hold Confirmation, Accelerated Weekly Settlement Monitoring Reports (`SM-BLKC-2026-Rev15+`), and Remedial Foundation Submittals** — Required from **Steven Kendrow (Project Executive), Marcus Whitfield (Superintendent), and Dennis Halloran, PLS (Survey Party Chief), Rowan Bay Constructors, Inc.** per `Spec 31 20 00` Art. 3.6.B–C.
